blocks.content: HP has 12 districts reorganised on 1 September 1972 from the original 4 districts. They are grouped into 3 administrative divisions.
On 1st September 1972, Himachal Pradesh was reorganized into 12 administrative districts, establishing the modern territorial framework of the state.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Himachal Pradesh was initially formed on April 15, 1948, by integrating 30 princely states into 4 core districts: Chamba, Mahasu, Mandi, and Sirmour.
Bilaspur was merged as the 5th district on July 1, 1954, and Kinnaur became the 6th district on May 1, 1960.
The major territorial expansion occurred during the Punjab Reorganization on November 1, 1966, adding Kangra, Kullu, Lahaul & Spiti, and Shimla.
On September 1, 1972, the state was reorganized into its present structure of 12 districts with the creation of Una, Hamirpur, and Solan.
Lahaul & Spiti covers the largest geographical area (24.85% of HP), while Kangra holds the highest population.
Original 1948 Districts: Memorize the four foundational districts—Chamba, Mahasu, Mandi, and Sirmour.
Area Extremes: Lahaul & Spiti is the largest district by area (13,835 sq km), whereas Hamirpur is the smallest (1,118 sq km).
Demographic Extremes: Kangra has the highest population, while Lahaul & Spiti has the lowest population density (2 persons per sq km).
Literacy Leader: Hamirpur consistently records the highest literacy rate among all districts in Himachal Pradesh.
